title: bthci_vendor: Android specific update
description:
Hi ! I propose such changes to bthci-vendor:

- the first commit is an update of an already existing Broadcom vendor command: LE Get Vendor Capabilities, which contain Android specific data
- the second commit is the Broadcom dissector support of: https://source.android.com/docs/core/connect/bluetooth/hci_requirements#a2dp-hardware-offload-support
- the third commit is a separate Android specific dissector which may be enabled/disabled in Edit>Preferences>Advanced. It is a controller-agnostic dissector that conforms with HCI requirements from Android: https://source.android.com/docs/core/connect/bluetooth/hci_requirements. Not all commands are fully supported yet and they will need to be added later on.

Please let me know if anything should be changed, thank you!

I don't see the point of the preference. There is already a vendor payload table that is empty by default, and that table is tried first before the vendor from the manufacturer.

This Android dissector was added to that table. If the Android dissector is selected in that payload table via Decode As, then it is always used instead of the manufacturer, same as the preference.

We don't want a bunch of redundant per dissector preferences when there's already a perfectly serviceable Decode As table that can be saved and does the same thing. As the preference has not been in a released version, I would suggest removing it before 4.6.0 is released and just using the Decode As payload table.
Hi! Could you explain in more detail how without using this preference one can force wireshark to decode as bthci_vendor.android rather than bthci_vendor.broadcom or bthci_vendor.intel? Thank you!

Sure! If you open up the Decode As window (either from Analyze->Decode As (Ctrl-Shift-U) in the top menu or from right-clicking in the packet list and selecting "Decode As"), a window like this pops up:

![image](/uploads/3f0640be26ac77233b94bdcd176451ef/image.png)

On the left most column, there is a list of tables. Select the "BT HCI Vendor" table. Then under the rightmost "Current" column, select "HCI Android" from the list of options:

![image](/uploads/7a1afc9e098e3e220845400b425067b3/image.png)

Then click "OK" to use that setting for the current Wireshark session, or "Save" to save the Decode As table entries to your current profile for future Wireshark sessions as well. (This also creates a file in your profile that is possible to edit manually.)

This is the first table that is tried for Vendor-specific Command Opcodes and Event Codes (and Command Complete and Command Status event codes that have Vendor-specific Command Opcodes in them), before the manufacturer is looked up. By default this table has no entry, which means that it is ignored and the manufacturer lookup table is used instead. If the entry in this table is the Android vendor dissector, then it will always be used without doing the manufacturer lookup, the same as your preference.
Thank you ! So we definitely do not need the preference switch. I lacked knowledge about Decode As ;)
